data.name: Seamless_Cursor_Name
data.comment: Seamless Multi-Screen Cursor is a product name of a PowerToys Mouse Utility.

data.name: Overlay_Instructions_Align
data.value: Each border between two monitors has two numbered pairs of lines in its color. Drag the lines of each pair until together they look like one straight line running across the bezel. Keep pair 1 and pair 2 far apart.
data.comment: First paragraph of the calibration instructions. Lines are colored markers along the edges of each monitor.

data.name: Overlay_Instructions_Try
data.value: Try while adjusting: move the pointer across a border to check the result before you save. With Pointer trail on, move it straight across: its trail should look straight.
data.comment: Second paragraph of the calibration instructions. "Try while adjusting" is the name of a switch in the same panel.

data.name: Overlay_Instructions_Switches
data.value: To keep the usual Windows behavior at a border, turn its Smooth crossing switch off. To let the pointer cross a gap between two monitors that face each other, turn their Glue switch on.
data.comment: Third paragraph of the calibration instructions. "Smooth crossing" and "Glue" are names of switches on the monitors.

data.name: Overlay_Key_Tab
data.value: Tab: next line, switch or button
data.comment: Keyboard hint, kept on one line. Tab is a key name.

data.name: Overlay_Key_Arrows
data.value: Arrow keys: move the line (Shift: faster)
data.comment: Keyboard hint, kept on one line. Shift is a key name.

data.name: Overlay_Key_Space
data.comment: Keyboard hint, kept on one line. Space is a key name; "press" means using the switch or button that Tab selected.

data.name: Overlay_Key_Enter
data.comment: Keyboard hint, kept on one line. Enter is a key name.

data.name: Overlay_Key_Esc
data.comment: Keyboard hint, kept on one line. Esc is a key name.

data.name: Overlay_No_Borders
data.value: No monitors share a border. Arrange the monitors so they touch in Windows display settings, then calibrate again.
data.comment: Shown in the calibration panel when no two monitors touch.

data.name: Overlay_Save
data.comment: Button

data.name: Overlay_Reset
data.comment: Button that puts all lines back to their predicted positions

data.name: Overlay_Cancel
data.comment: Button

data.name: Overlay_Close
data.comment: Button

data.name: Overlay_Crossing_On
data.comment: Switch for one border between two monitors, in its on state. Keep it short: it is shown on a fixed-width switch.

data.name: Overlay_Crossing_Off
data.comment: Switch for one border between two monitors, in its off state. Keep it short: it is shown on a fixed-width switch.

data.name: Overlay_Issue_Too_Close
data.value: The pairs are close together. Move them further apart for better precision.
data.comment: Warning shown next to a border. A pair is two lines, one on each monitor.

data.name: Overlay_Issue_Invalid
data.value: Two lines are at the same spot. This border is not used until they are apart.
data.comment: Error shown next to a border

data.name: Overlay_Issue_Reversed
data.value: The lines are in a different order on the two screens. This border is not used until that is fixed.
data.comment: Error shown next to a border

data.name: Overlay_Issue_Scale
data.value: The lines do not match a plausible screen size. This border is not used until they do.
data.comment: Error shown next to a border

data.name: Overlay_Save_Failed
data.value: Saving failed. Try again, or press Esc to close without saving.
data.comment: Esc is a key name

data.name: Overlay_Save_Blocked
data.value: Cannot save, because the saved calibration could not be read. Press Esc, then open the calibration again.
data.comment: Esc is a key name

data.name: Overlay_Preview_On
data.comment: Switch in its on state. Keep it short: it is shown on a fixed-width switch.

data.name: Overlay_Preview_Off
data.comment: Switch in its off state. Keep it short: it is shown on a fixed-width switch.

data.name: Overlay_Glue_On
data.comment: Switch in its on state. {0} is the name of the other monitor. Keep it short: it is shown on a fixed-width switch.

data.name: Overlay_Glue_Off
data.comment: Switch in its off state. {0} is the name of the other monitor. Keep it short: it is shown on a fixed-width switch.

data.name: Overlay_Map_On
data.comment: Switch in its on state. Keep it short: it is shown on a fixed-width switch.

data.name: Overlay_Map_Off
data.comment: Switch in its off state. Keep it short: it is shown on a fixed-width switch.

data.name: Overlay_Trail_On
data.comment: Switch in its on state: the pointer leaves fading dots behind it. Keep it short: it is shown on a fixed-width switch.

data.name: Overlay_Trail_Off
data.comment: Switch in its off state. Keep it short: it is shown on a fixed-width switch.

data.name: Overlay_Stop_On
data.comment: Switch in its on state: the pointer stops where no monitor is physically across. Keep it short: it is shown on a fixed-width switch.

data.name: Overlay_Stop_Off
data.comment: Switch in its off state. Keep it short: it is shown on a fixed-width switch.

data.name: Overlay_Map_Legend
data.value: Edge map: in the border's color, the pointer crosses. Red, it stops (CursorWrap can still wrap it at outer edges). No color, Windows decides.
data.comment: Legend for the colored strips along the monitor edges. CursorWrap is a product name of another Mouse Utility.

data.name: Setting_Stop_At_Empty_Edges
data.value: Stop the pointer where no monitor is physically across
data.comment: Setting

data.name: Setting_Map_Cursor_Wrap
data.value: Keep the physical position when CursorWrap wraps the pointer
data.comment: Setting. CursorWrap is a product name of another Mouse Utility.

data.name: Overlay_Monitors_Unknown
data.value: Windows does not report which monitors are connected right now, for example in a remote session, so they cannot be calibrated. Try again later.
data.comment: Shown in the calibration panel instead of the instructions.
